text: Data Analyst basics: difference between INNER, LEFT, RIGHT and FULL joins; GROUP BY vs HAVING; window functions like ROW_NUMBER and RANK; handling NULLs and duplicates; how to clean a messy dataset in pandas.

Machine learning basics: bias-variance tradeoff, overfitting and how to prevent it, precision vs recall vs F1, train/validation/test split, cross-validation, when to use accuracy vs ROC-AUC on imbalanced data.

GenAI and LLM basics: what is RAG and why use it over fine-tuning, how chunking size affects retrieval, what embeddings are, how to reduce hallucinations, prompt engineering techniques like few-shot and chain-of-thought, how to evaluate an LLM app.

Behavioral: tell me about yourself, your biggest challenge in a project, a time you disagreed with a teammate, a failure and what you learned. Answer in STAR format: Situation, Task, Action, Result with a measurable outcome.

Python and DSA basics: list vs tuple vs set vs dict, time complexity of dict lookup, two pointers and hashmap patterns, reverse a linked list, detect a cycle, explain recursion vs iteration, decorators and generators.

Resume project deep-dive: why did you choose this model or library, what was the dataset size, what were the trade-offs, how did you measure success, what would you change if you had more time, how would you deploy it and scale it.
TCS typical process: online aptitude and coding test (NQT), then Technical Interview, Managerial Interview and HR round. Technical round focuses on your own projects and academic basics.

TCS technical round themes: explain your final-year project in detail, OOP concepts (inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation), DBMS (normalization, keys, joins, ACID), basic SQL queries, one programming language of your choice such as C, Java or Python.
TCS HR round themes: willingness to relocate and work in shifts, why TCS, strengths and weaknesses, where do you see yourself in 5 years, how you handle pressure, communication clarity.
Infosys typical process: online assessment (InfyTQ or similar: logical reasoning, math, verbal, pseudocode, coding), then technical interview and HR round.

Infosys technical themes: DBMS and SQL queries, OOP, data structures like arrays, stacks, queues, basic algorithms, puzzles and logical reasoning, explaining projects and internships, software testing and SDLC basics.
Infosys HR themes: why Infosys, flexibility with location and technology, teamwork example, learning ability, how you keep your skills updated.
Wipro typical process: online aptitude, written communication and coding assessment, followed by technical and HR interviews.
Wipro technical themes: programming fundamentals, OOP, DBMS and SQL, basic data structures, project explanation, and for analytics roles Excel, SQL and basic statistics.

Deloitte analyst-style process: online aptitude and technical assessment, a case or group-discussion style round for some roles, then technical and HR or partner interviews with emphasis on communication.

Deloitte data analytics themes: SQL joins and aggregations, Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP), Power BI or Tableau dashboards, explain a KPI you would track for a business problem, basic statistics like mean, median, standard deviation, correlation vs causation.

Deloitte case-style questions: a retail client has falling sales, how would you structure the analysis, which data would you ask for, which metrics would you check, how would you present insights to a non-technical stakeholder.
Accenture typical process: cognitive and technical assessment, coding questions, a communication assessment, then a technical and HR interview.
Accenture technical themes: cloud and networking fundamentals, DBMS and SQL, OOP, one programming language, MS Office or Excel basics, and your project or internship experience.
Accenture behavioral themes: adaptability to new technologies, working in diverse teams, client communication, handling tight deadlines, ethics and integrity scenarios.

Amazon typical process: online assessment with coding and work-style questions, then multiple interviews mixing data structures and algorithms with Leadership Principles behavioral questions, often including a bar raiser.

Amazon Leadership Principles questions: Customer Obsession, Ownership, Invent and Simplify, Dive Deep, Bias for Action, Deliver Results. Example: tell me about a time you took ownership beyond your role. Expect deep follow-ups on exactly what YOU did and the measurable result.
Amazon technical themes: arrays, strings, hashmaps, trees, graphs, sliding window and two pointers, complexity analysis, and for data roles advanced SQL with window functions and metrics design.
Google typical process: recruiter screen, then several technical interviews focused on problem solving, data structures and algorithms, and a behavioral or Googleyness round.

Google technical themes: algorithms and data structures with clear complexity analysis, thinking aloud, handling edge cases, optimizing a brute-force solution, and for ML roles probability, statistics and model evaluation fundamentals.
Google behavioral themes: handling ambiguity, collaboration, intellectual humility, how you learn from feedback, leading without authority.
Startup interviews are usually shorter with a practical task or take-home: build a small working feature or analysis, then discuss your design decisions with a founder or senior engineer.

Startup themes: ship fast with trade-offs, end-to-end ownership (data, model, API, deployment), GenAI app building with LangChain or LlamaIndex, RAG evaluation, cost and latency of LLM calls, debugging a production issue.
Startup behavioral themes: ownership, comfort with ambiguity, wearing multiple hats, how you prioritize when everything is urgent, a project you built on your own initiative.
